paragraphs.en: Players face an automatic dealer with six freshly shuffled decks. Number cards keep their value, faces count ten and each ace counts one or eleven. The aim is to beat the dealer without exceeding 21. All chips belong only to this table.

A win returns the stake plus an equal profit. An original two-card 21 pays a profit of 3:2. Matching dealer and player naturals push. A natural beats an ordinary 21. A bust loses even if the dealer later busts. Half-chip payouts are exact.

Each round starts with an automatic opening contribution from every active player: ten chips by default, or the table setting. A player with less pays their entire balance and is all-in. Then players act in seat order: check if nothing is owed, call a raise, raise, fold, or go all-in. A raise makes the others respond again. Betting closes when all players who still have chips have responded and matched the current bet, or only one player has not folded. All-in players keep their right to play without further betting. A short all-in does not reopen raising for someone who already acted unless the cumulative increase reaches a full raise.

Use C to check or call, F to fold, A for all-in, and R or B to type your own raise. The entered amount is the increase above the current bet; any amount needed to call is added to the payment. Raises start at one chip and later must match the last full raise; a smaller final all-in is allowed. Preset raises are also in the actions list. Cards or dice start only after betting closes.

Choose Hit or Stand in the actions list. In the extended variant, the original two-card hand can be doubled, receiving exactly one further card, or a matching-rank pair can be split once into two hands. Each requires an additional stake. Split aces receive one card each and stop; split hands never earn the natural bonus. There is no insurance, surrender, resplitting or double after splitting.

The dealer reveals the hole card after all player decisions, then draws below 17 and stands on every 17, including soft 17. Player cards are open. The ordinary interface conceals the dealer hole card; the shared deterministic replay is not protection against a modified client. Bots use only their hand and the dealer upcard.

Choose Simple or Extended, rounds (1–100), initial chips (10–10000) and the opening contribution. Defaults are ten rounds, 100 chips and an opening contribution of ten. The dealer settles each remaining player’s actual hand stake separately; a fold loses the chips already paid. The last player after other folds still plays against the dealer. Any positive balance may fund a short all-in next round. The highest final balance wins; tied maxima draw. Previously recorded games keep their original betting rules.

The social variant has no house hand. Players take turns dealing, rotating the dealing seat every round. After the common ante and betting round, the dealing player presses D to deal. Everyone plays against the other players, with ordinary hit/stand decisions. There is no splitting, doubling, house payout or natural bonus. Contribution levels form pots; the highest eligible total up to 21 wins each layer, and exact ties split it. If all eligible hands bust, that layer is refunded. Chips are conserved. The dealer plays last and the next round moves to the next solvent seat. This is the Power Games social format, not the casino bank game.
paragraphs.pl: Ta odmiana nie ma ręki krupiera. Gracze rozdają kolejno, a rozdający zmienia się co rundę. Po wspólnym wpisowym i licytacji rozdający naciska D. Wszyscy grają przeciw sobie, dobierając lub zatrzymując rękę. Nie ma podziału par, podwajania, wypłaty banku ani premii za naturalnego blackjacka. Wpłaty tworzą pule; każdą wygrywa najwyższy uprawniony wynik do 21, a remisy dzielą pulę. Jeśli wszystkie uprawnione ręce przekroczą 21, warstwa wraca do wpłacających. Suma żetonów się nie zmienia. Rozdający gra ostatni; następna runda przechodzi do kolejnego wypłacalnego miejsca. To format towarzyski Power Games.

paragraphs.en: Use the arrows to choose an action and Enter to perform it. Tab changes fields. T reads the current turn; S reads scores. F1 opens the current shortcut reference; Ctrl+F1 opens the rules. Card hands preserve physical card identity and draw order. Their cards are for inspection, not play: choose decisions in the separate actions list.
